chapter: Armstrong, Parker and life inside the Basie band
title: Why many older musicians put bebop down
summary: Tate liked the bebop players, but did not try to play that way, and cannot see why others put it down.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: Then, of course, he continued to play. I mean, we'd jam down there at night and he was playing -- by then, he was playing what he wanted -- his style then, you know, but it hadn't really caught on with the people.
The bebop thing wasn't really such a tremendous revolution?
No, I heard Buster Smith do it, I really did, you know.
But a lot of older musicians were disturbed by it.

Well, yeah, actually, it's a different -- it's different from a lot of old musicians that play with -- that don't play many notes, you understand, and play like from here. It's a different thing. Sometime I wonder how Herschel would have been. He wouldn't have been in that school. Like Ben didn't ever get in that school and, you know, I never was really into that. But I really could have, you know, if I really wanted -- really tried. But I don't know, I just don't feel all the way that way.
No, I can see why you wouldn't, you know, you had an established style and you wouldn't want to play like somebody else. But I've always been curious about why so many musicians kind of put it down.

Well, you know, I never -- I can't either understand that. Because I think it's maybe jealousy, because it's -- you can't put them down, because they can play, you know what I mean? And if you listen to it, it's -- you know, just like Bird swung and carried melody all -- you know, because you always knew where he was, you know. It's some things today that really scares me, that hangs me up, you know. But not like Bird and them played, I mean, I always knew what they were doing and I really dug people that played like Bird and, you know, what they called the bebop. I dug it, really. I just didn't really try to get into it, because I don't think
-- I think I would have lost something if I had. But I -- it wasn't because I really didn't dig it. Because I dug those cats, man.
